questions.q: What does BACKUP DATABASE ... WITH DIFFERENTIAL actually capture?
options: Everything changed since the last full backup
Only the transaction log since the last log backup
An exact duplicate of the last full backup
Only schema changes, not data
questions.explain: A differential backup captures all data changed since the most recent full backup, staying smaller and faster than another full.

questions.q: Under which recovery model(s) can BACKUP LOG be used?
options: FULL or BULK_LOGGED
SIMPLE only
Any recovery model
None — BACKUP LOG requires Always Encrypted
questions.explain: SIMPLE recovery truncates the log automatically and maintains no log backup chain; log backups require FULL or BULK_LOGGED recovery model.

questions.q: What does the CHECKSUM option on a BACKUP DATABASE statement do?
options: Detects page-level corruption during the backup operation itself
Encrypts the backup file
Compresses the backup file
Verifies the login's permissions before backing up
questions.explain: CHECKSUM is cheap insurance that catches corruption while the backup is being taken, rather than discovering it only at restore time.

questions.q: What does the frequency of transaction log backups directly control?
options: The Recovery Point Objective (RPO) — how much data loss is acceptable
The database's recovery model
Whether differential backups are allowed
The fixed server role of the backup operator
questions.explain: Since log backups capture the ongoing stream of transactions, their frequency directly caps how much data could be lost in a disaster — the RPO.

questions.q: In a rotation of Sunday full + nightly differential + frequent log backups, what does restoring to the most recent point require?
options: The last full backup, the most recent differential, and every log backup taken after that differential
Only the most recent log backup
Every log backup since Sunday, ignoring the differential entirely
Only the full backup — differentials and logs are not needed
questions.explain: The differential lets you skip applying every log since the full; you apply the full, the latest differential, then only the logs taken after that differential.
